chunks: The number of his teachers reached more than fifty persons from the notables of both groups.

key_terms.أَعْلَامِ: notables/prominent figures — senior scholars of recognized standing in their communities
key_terms.الْفَرِيقَيْنِ: the two groups — the Shia and Sunni scholarly communities
key_terms.مَشَايِخِهِ: his shaykhs/teachers — scholars under whom he formally studied and received ijaza

ai.seo_question: How many teachers did Shaykh al-Tusi (Shaykh al-Ta'ifa) have, and from which scholarly traditions did they come?
ai.summary: This entry from the biographical chapter on Shaykh al-Ṭā'ifa (Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī, 385–460 AH) records that he formally studied under more than fifty prominent scholars. Remarkably, these teachers came from both the Shia and Sunni scholarly traditions, attesting to the breadth of his learning and his standing in the cosmopolitan academic milieu of 5th-century AH Baghdad.
